THIS MFA FILED U/S 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 23.10.2010 PASSED IN MVC NO.7604/2009 ON THE FILE OF VII ADDITIONAL JUDGE,
COURT OF SMALL CAUSES, MEMBER, MACT-3, BANGALORE,
AWARDING A COMPENSATION OF Rs.4,04,000/- WITH INTEREST @ 6% P.A. FROM THE DATE OF PETITION TILL DEPOSIT AND ETC.
 THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed under Section-173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'MV Act' for brevity) by the appellant-insurance company, calling in question the judgment and award dated 23.10.2010, passed in M.V.C.No.7604/2009, on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal' for brevity) on the ground that respondent No.1 who is the owner of the motor cycle in question bearing registration no.KA-03-EV-1850, hence, he cannot make the claim against himself.
Another ground is that claimant No.2 is the mother of the deceased and is not depending on the income of the deceased as the deceased was married daughter of Respondent No.2 - claimant No.2.
Therefore, on these two grounds prays to set-aside the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
Brief facts.

2. On 03.10.2009, at about 9.30 p.m., deceased R. Shwetha was returning to Nelamangala after visiting the Anjaneya Swamy Temple near Tavarekere, Huliyur Durga Hobli, and was riding as a pillion rider in motor bike bearing No.KA-03-EU-1850 which was being ridden by R.J.Harish,
relative of deceased.

When they reached near Belagumba near Gudemarenahalli-Magadi Road, the rider rode the said motor bike in high speed in rash and negligent way and hence the deceased fell M/S Oriental Insurance Co Ltd vs Ashok Rao S/O Late Nanjunda Rao on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86564401/
2 down and sustained injuries all over the body.

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Co Ltd vs Ashok Rao
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Immediately he was shifted to Harsha Hospital,
Nelamangala for first aid and later on next day i.e., on 04.10.2009 at about 2.30 a.m., deceased succumbed to the injuries.
3. Hence, a claim petition was filed by the claimants under Section-166 of the M.V. Act, claiming compensation for the death of the deceased in the road traffic accident.

The Tribunal on appreciating the materials on record, allowed the claim petition in part, and awarded a compensation of Rs.4,04,000/-, along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realisation.
The Tribunal held respondent No.2 therein, liable to pay the compensation.

4. Heard arguments of the learned counsel for the parties and perused the materials on record.
5.
In the present case, the claimants are the husband and mother of the deceased.

The deceased while riding as a pillion rider in the motor cycle bearing No.KA- 03-EU-1850, which was ridden by the friend of claimant No.1 met with an accident and the deceased succumbed to the injuries.
The claimant no.1 before the Tribunal is respondent No.1 herein.
6. It is not disputed fact that claimant no.1 who is the husband of the deceased, was the owner of the motor cycle in question
. The husband of the deceased was examined as PW-1.
In his cross-examination he has clearly admitted that he is owner of motor cycle No.KA-03-EU- 1850.
Therefore, claimant no.1 being husband of the deceased cannot maintain the claim made against himself.
Therefore, so far as claimant no.1 before the Tribunal who is also respondent No.1 is not entitled for compensation.
In this regard, the Tribunal has committed error in entertaining the claim petition filed by claimant No.1.
7. Claimant No.1, who has lost his wife is also arraigned as respondent No.1, being owner of the motor cycle.
Therefore, the claimant cannot make claim against himself.
In this regard, the Tribunal had committed error in entertaining the claim petition in so far as claimant No.1, who is husband of the deceased.
8. So far as the claimant No.2, viz., Bhagya Bai is concerned who is mother of the deceased.

In other words, claimant no.2 who is mother-in-law of claimant no.1 it is the submission made by the learned counsel for the insurance company that the deceased is married to the claimant No.1 and was residing separately along with her husband, therefore claimant no.2 was not depending on the income of the deceased.

Further, referring to the cross-examination that the claimant no.2 was residing separately, therefore claimant No.2 is neither entitled for compensation under the head 'loss of dependency' nor entitled under the head 'loss of estate'.

9. The learned counsel for the claimant relied on the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Manjuri Bera vs Oriental Insurance Company Limited1 (hereinafter referred to as 'Manjuri Bera' for brevity).

entities.text: Manjuri Bera vs Oriental Insurance Company Limited1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Admittedly, the claimant No.2 is a widow.
In the course of cross-examination of PW-1 who is husband of deceased had stated that the claimant No.2 has two other daughters who are unmarried.

Even though strictly it cannot be construed that the claimant No.2 is depending on the income of the deceased, but the fact remains proved that the claimant No.2 is a widower having two M/S Oriental Insurance Co Ltd vs Ashok Rao S/O Late Nanjunda Rao on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86564401/

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Co Ltd vs Ashok Rao
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3 other daughters.
10. Further, even though the deceased was married to claimant No.1, but the deceased was having two unmarried sisters at the time of the accident.

Therefore, claimant No.2 filed the claim petition for claiming compensation and the tribunal has granted compensation under the head 'loss of estate'
but not under the head 'loss of dependency'.
Whether claimant No.2 is entitled for compensation under the head 'loss of estate' 2007 (10) SCC 643 as awarded by the Tribunal is a question to be considered here.
11. As per Section-166 of the MV Act, a claim petition can be filed by the legal representatives of the deceased.
There is distinction between 'legal representatives' and 'legal heirs'.
Legal heirs can be both 'legal heirs' and 'legal representatives', but legal representatives may not be in all cases 'legal heirs'.
But under Section-166 of MV Act, the words used is 'legal representative' can maintain claim petition.

12. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Manjuri Bera's referred to supra, while referring Section- 2(11) of CPC and Section-2(1)(g) of Arbitration and Conciliation Act 1996, were pleased to observe at para-11 and 12 of the judgment as follows:
"11.
There are several factors which have to be noted.
The liability under Section 140 of the Act does not cease because there is absence of dependency.
The right to file a claim application has to be considered in the background of right to entitlement.
While assessing the quantum, the multiplier system is applied because of deprivation of dependency.
In other words, multiplier is a measure.
There are three stages while assessing the question of entitlement.
Firstly, the liability of the person who is liable and the person who is to indemnify the liability, if any.
Next is the quantification and Section 166 is primarily in the nature of recovery proceedings.

As noted above,
liability in terms of Section 140 of the Act does not cease because of absence of dependency.
Section 165 of the Act also throws some light on the controversy.

The explanation includes the liability under Sections 140 and 163A.
12.
Judged in that background where a legal representative who is not dependant files an application for compensation, the quantum cannot be less than the liability referable to Section 140 of the Act.

Therefore, even if there is no loss of dependency the claimant if he or she is a legal representative will be entitled to compensation, the quantum of which shall be not less than the liability flowing from Section 140 of the Act.
The appeal is allowed to the aforesaid extent.
There will be no order as to costs.
We record our appreciation for the able assistance - 10 - rendered by Shri Jayant Bhushan, the learned Amicus Curiae."

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Co Ltd vs Ashok Rao
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the above cited case, the married sister filed a claim petition on account of death of another sister.
Under these circumstances, it was held by the Hon'ble Apex Court that the claim petition filed by the married sister is by virtue as a 'legal representatives'.
Hence, can maintain claim petition but awarded compensation under 'no fault liability theory' as per Section-140 of the MV Act.

Therefore,
the term 'legal representative' has wider meaning compared to legal heir.
Therefore, the claim petition filed by the mother of the deceased as claimant No.2 as a legal representative of the deceased is hence maintainable as per definition above stated.

14. The factual matrix involved in the above said Manjuri Bera's case is concerned, so far as the ground of compensation granted under Section-140 of the MV Act is not applicable in the present case for the reason that in the above stated case, the claimant was a married sister.
- 11 - Therefore, the married sister neither depending on the deceased nor entitled to represent the estate of the deceased.

Therefore, granted compensation only under Section-140 of the MV Act, due to difference of factual matrix involved in the above stated case and in the present case, the same is not applicable in the present case, so far as entitlement of compensation under no fault liability, but the principle legal representative is applicable.
15. In the above present case, the claimant is mother of the deceased and widow having two other unmarried daughters.
Even though claimant No.2 being mother is residing separately in separate village that does not mean that the mother is not entitled for 'loss of estate'.

Quite naturally,
claimant No.2 is mother of deceased and widow has responsibility of looking after and bringing up two other unmarried daughters.
Therefore, the deceased must have been contributing some income to claimant no.2 till her life time.

Claimant No.2 is having two other unmarried daughters, it is quite natural that the deceased being married daughters was supposed to take little bit care by giving financial help to some extent as the deceased was having two unmarried daughters.
Therefore, it can be construed as the mother is representing the estate of the deceased to some extent.
Therefore, the compensation granted by the Tribunal to claimant No.2 under the head 'loss of estate' is correct and justified.
17. The Tribunal has calculated the compensation under the head 'loss of estate' and accordingly awarded compensation apportioning between the husband (claimant No.1) and mother (claimant No.2).
But as above stated, claimant No.1 being husband of the deceased is also owner of the motor cycle No.KA-03-EU- 1850, cannot maintain claim against himself.
Therefore, the claim petition so far as against the claimant No.1 is dismissed as discussed above.

Therefore, the claimant no.2 being mother of the deceased is entitled for - 13 - M/S Oriental Insurance Co Ltd vs Ashok Rao S/O Late Nanjunda Rao on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86564401/
5 compensation under the head 'loss of estate' and that is correctly determined.

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Co Ltd vs Ashok Rao S/O Late Nanjunda Rao
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: But the claimant No.2 is entitled for full compensation under the head 'loss of estate' and that is correctly determined by the Tribunal.
To this extent, the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is modified.
But the contention raised by the insurance company that claimant no.2 being the mother of the deceased is not entitled for compensation
is liable to be rejected.
18. If at all the deceased was alive, then she would have been contributing to the mother, since the mother is a widow having responsibility of looking after two other unmarried daughters.

Therefore,
on the death of the deceased the mother is entitled for 'loss of estate'.
Therefore, in this regard the mother is entitled for compensation under the head loss of estate, and that is correctly held and calculated by the Tribunal.
Hence, the appeal filed by the Insurance Company is found to be devoid of merits.
Hence, is liable to be dismissed.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i.
The appeal is Dismissed.
ii. The impugned judgment and award dated 23.10.2010, passed in M.V.C.No.7604/2009, on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru is Upheld.
iii. Claimant No.2 - appellant No.2, mother of the deceased is entitled for compensation under the head loss of estate, as held by the Tribunal.
iv. The remaining observations and findings made by the Tribunal in the aforesaid impugned judgment and award are kept in tact.
v. The amount in deposit by the Insurance company shall be transferred to the Tribunal forthwith.
Registry is directed to return the Trial Court Records to the Tribunal, along with certified copy of the order passed by this Court forthwith without any delay.
vii. No order as to costs.
